body:
Lauren,

I applaud your interest in this topic - the Unabomber story has so many
intriguing elements to it.

In the essay, "Industrial Society and its Future", aka the Unabomber Manifesto,
Ted Kaczynski makes a number of arguments to prove his point that "The
Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for the human
race". 

He argues that, to be happy, people need goals and some chance of attaining
their goals. They also need personal control over their own lives, which is
generally slipping away from people. He talks about the powerful industrial
technological society's role in breaking down the family. He also discusses the
feelings of purposelessness that people have in today's world, and the
consequences, such as addiction to things like drugs, TV, spending money you
don't have, which modern people use to get themselves through their lives.

You might want to use some of those themes, and tie them in with your
observations about people and things in the news. For example, a few months
ago, on 20/20 or 60 minutes or one of those, there was a segment about heroin
addiction amongst high school students in a well off town in Texas, and there
had been a rash of suicides there a few years earlier, which also made the
news. I wish I had more specific info.

In the "manifesto", look up paragraphs 37, 42, 50, 51, 66 and footnote 21, for
starters, although if you are going to take on this rather complicated theme,
there are many more related paragraphs.

Another intersting theme might be the way technology starts out as optional,
and then becomes necessary. You might want to explore the effects on the
environment, or on people. An example out of the manifesto relates to the
automobile. Most people didn't own one when they first came out, but now most
people couldn't do without one. We can get to travel much more than our
ancestors, but we also have air pollution, the stress of being in traffic every
day, and dangerous rude drivers to contend with. Another example is the built
in obsolecense of most products that we are encouraged to buy.  You might want
to think about other examples, and discuss those, and their effects. See
paragraph 127 of the manifesto.

There was also a section called, "The 'Bad' Parts of Technology Cannot be
Separated from the 'Good' Parts". How do you see the balance between the good
and bad parts of technology? I refer you to a Washington Post article about the
intrusion of database technology into people's lives. You might want to reflect
on this and other subjects that you can think of.

See paragraphs 121 - 124 of the manifesto, and 

http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/WPlate/1998-03/10/084l-031098-idx.html

Yet another idea - the difference between "freedom" and "permissiveness",
discussed in paragraphs 94 and 72, and elsewhere. What would life be like if
people people were truly free, instead of being granted "freedom" by some
power? How much real freedom do we have?

Of course, Dr. Kaczynski addressed many issues about modern life, which are all
related to each other, just like a spider web - touch one thread and it affects
another. But, that is life.

My last suggestion, if you haven't done so already, is read the manifesto. You
very well might find a topic there that you find more interesting than those I
suggested. You can find it all over the net.

Two other interesting sites (for starters, there are plenty of others) on some
background information you may want:

http://www.unabombertrial.com/
http://www.paranoia.com/unapack/

Hope this helped and Good Luck on your paper!


SJJ
